hook: Two economies report the same real GDP growth this year. In one, factories have idle shifts and job ads are scarce. In the other, firms are paying overtime and still cannot find workers. To tell them apart you need more than output: you need to know where output stands against what the economy can produce at full employment. The AD-AS model puts both on one graph.

options: A fall in the price level
A rise in the unemployment rate to zero
prereq.why: A recessionary (negative) gap is real GDP below potential (full-employment) output.

options: Horizontal at the current price level
prereq.why: In the long run output is at potential at any price level: LRAS is vertical at YF.

figure.caption: Left: AD meets SRAS left of LRAS, a recessionary gap. Right: AD meets SRAS right of LRAS, an inflationary gap.

chain.effect: the short-run price level (PL1) and real GDP (Y1) are set

chain.cause: Y1 is to the left of LRAS
chain.effect: a recessionary gap: unemployment above the natural rate

chain.cause: Y1 is to the right of LRAS
chain.effect: an inflationary gap: unemployment below the natural rate

chain.cause: AD and SRAS cross on LRAS

ideas: The AD-AS model puts AD, SRAS and LRAS on one graph: Price level (PL) up the side, Real GDP (Y) along the bottom.
Short-run equilibrium is where AD crosses SRAS; label it PL1 and Y1 with dashed lines to both axes.
Long-run equilibrium is where AD and SRAS cross on LRAS: output at full employment (YF), unemployment at the natural rate.
Y1 < YF: a recessionary gap, unemployment above the natural rate. Y1 > YF: an inflationary gap, unemployment below it.

misconception.wrong: Wherever AD crosses SRAS, the economy is at full employment, because that is the equilibrium.
misconception.right: AD crossing SRAS is only a short-run equilibrium. Output is at full employment only when that crossing lies on LRAS.

summary: The AD-AS model shows the price level and real GDP where AD meets SRAS (short-run equilibrium). Comparing that output with LRAS shows the gap: left of LRAS is a recessionary gap with unemployment above the natural rate, right of LRAS an inflationary gap with unemployment below it. Long-run equilibrium is where all three curves meet.
